conf: conf ON A RECORD IN THIS FILE GRADES THE ERRATUM AGAINST ITS GIT EVIDENCE, NEVER AGAINST ARDA. Every record's claim is about this archive -- 'on this date this dataset said X, and now says Y' -- and its evidence is a git blob, which is the most checkable evidence in the building. THE PRIOR READING IS ALWAYS VERBATIM: a record whose prior reading could not be recovered from the parent blob is not written at all, so no tier here means a doubtful `was`. The tier grades the REASON's distance from the record: [C] the commit that made the change names this record or names a token that moved in it; [I-H] the commit names the field and nothing narrower; [I-M] the commit states a reason for the commit and this record is one of the values it changed. [I-L], [EXT] and [NEO] are unused and would be meaningless here.
provenance: Mined from the site repository's own history by map/gen_errata.py. Every `was` is the verbatim string in the parent commit's blob at the named field; every `sha` is the commit that replaced it. map/errata_check.py re-opens each blob and refuses if any `was` is not found there, so a correction in this archive cannot be fabricated -- it can only be recovered.
method: A change is a CORRECTION when its assertive tokens moved -- its numbers, proper nouns, citation tokens or confidence marker -- a RETRACTION when the reading was emptied or its key removed, and a REFINEMENT when the prose moved and the assertive tokens did not. Refinements are counted and NOT written: no mark applies to them, and marking one would say the archive changed its mind when it changed its wording. The rule over-calls refinement on purpose.

errata.was: NAME-GLOSS ONLY. The corpus glosses this name, or the archive's registers bind a creature, plant or object to it -- and NOTHING in the corpus attaches that image to this subject AS A SIGN. Composing here would be invention, and this is the rule that kills the most tempting candidates: Ossiriand's seven rivers, Thargelion's Land Beyond Gelion, Dorwinion's wine, Framsburg's dragon-slaying founder. Every one would need a charge Tolkien never gave and, usually, an ordinary he never used. The evidence sweep found CO-OCCURRENCE ONLY: a blazon word standing near the name with nothing binding the two. On its own that supports a declared blank as readily as it supports a device.

errata.now: A place binding is made only where THIS ARCHIVE'S OWN gazetteer note, or the plate's own prompt, names the thing depicted as belonging to that place -- Shelob's tunnel and the Stairs of Cirith Ungol, Sauron's werewolf-keep at Tol Sirion, the chief palantir stood under its Dome of Stars at Osgiliath. A creature, plant, artefact or soldier bound this way is NOT a view of the place and must be captioned with its own subject from arda_assets, never as a picture of the route. THE ARCHIVE STILL HOLDS ONLY SIX ARCHITECTURAL VIEWS of any place -- art/pl_*.jpg -- and that is the real gap; it is closed by rendering arda_place_prompts, whose population is ten hand-typed rows against 168 MAN_MADE places (map/gen_place_prompts.py --candidates), and not by binding harder.

errata.now: CORRECTED 19 Aug 2026, and the earlier note here was wrong in the direction that manufactures work. It read that heraldry/gondor.svg, heraldry/redeye.svg and heraldry/rohan.svg are published with no row in arda_assets.json 'so the archive cannot state whose they are'. TRUE HALF: no heraldry file has a row in arda_assets.json -- all 38 published ones, not three. FALSE HALF: the archive states whose they are perfectly well, in site/arda_heraldry_assets.json, which carries author, licence, source, basis and sha1 for 121 devices; map/licence_check.py READS that second register and says in its own source why copying the rows across would be the WRONG fix -- 'two registers holding the same rows must be kept in step by hand, which is the homograph fault this archive retires keys for'. So licence_check being green over them is correct and is not the silence the old note took it for. Right: run at 300 dpi over Baynes's paintings, tesseract returned `he "ghJay is ended` for `Day is ended` -- every stanza's decorated initial defeats it. Too narrow twice. First, the argument was about a MACHINE reading, and it never considered a reader looking at the plate; all twelve verse plates were read directly, and the tesseract pass kept only as a second opinion. Second, the diacritic argument does not actually reach this poem: THERE IS NOT ONE ACCENTED CHARACTER IN ITS 24 LINES, so the specific destruction measured was of forms this text does not contain. The metrical division is corroborated by the book's own structure rather than assumed -- twelve verse plates in three groups of four, two metrical lines a plate, giving 3 stanzas of 8 and couplet rhyme throughout -- and the printed display layout is preserved plate by plate beneath the poem so the source's own form is not lost. path: q=How do Orcs reproduce — and are there female Orcs?
errata.now: HoME X says they 'had life and multiplied after the manner of the Children of Ilúvatar', and Myths Transformed in the same volume says a good deal more. They 'bred and multiplied rapidly whenever left undisturbed'; they 'needed food and drink, and rest'; and their lifespan is stated outright — 'they died and were not immortal, even according to the manner of the Quendi; indeed they appear to have been by nature short-lived compared with the span of Men of higher race, such as the Edain'. One mode of breeding is named too, of Men reduced to the Orc-level: 'they would or could be made to mate with Orcs, producing new breeds, often larger and more cunning'. What is genuinely undescribed is a female Orc — no she-orc, orc-woman or orc-mother appears as whole words anywhere in Tolkien's own texts — the tier-1 and tier-2 shelf, which is the only place a silence about what he wrote can be established. FOUR TIER-3 WORKS DO USE THE TERMS, and every one of them agrees the description is absent rather than supplying it: Picturing Tolkien, which states that neither Tolkien nor Jackson portrays Orc women, The Complete Guide ('Nothing is said about Orkish tribal structures or female Orcs'), Shippey, who asks why readers never encounter them, and Mallorn 54, which canvasses a speculative parthenogenesis reading. They are second readers agreeing with us, not witnesses to the legendarium.

errata.was: [I-M] the archive's own reading. NO ANNAL DATES THIS GRANT. 410 is a date TYPED IN THE MARGIN of a Later Quenta typescript, reported by Christopher Tolkien: HoME XI, commentary on LQ §31 — 'The date of this gift, as typed in the margin, was 410'. errata.was: [I-M] the archive's own reading. NO ANNAL DATES THIS REMOVAL. Grey Annals §132 (year header 422) does grant Brethil by Thingol's leave — 'Here at the prayer of Inglor Thingol granted to Haleth's people to live in Brethil' — BUT CHRISTOPHER TOLKIEN DISQUALIFIES IT FOR THIS RECORD IN HIS OWN WORDS: 'Haleth here is of course Haleth the Hunter, who had entered Beleriand two years before' (HoME XI, commentary on Of the Coming of Men into the West §29). The Lady Haleth's Haladin do not occur in the Grey Annals text at all — 'Haladin' 0 times. The only dates are TYPED MARGINS on the LQ 1 typescript: the stockade siege 375, the Estolad sojourn 376–390, the crossing of the Brithiach 391, Haleth's death 420. AND 390 IS THE END OF THE SOJOURN, NOT THE REMOVAL — the crossing is margined 391, and Thingol's grace carries no date at all. The strictest true statement is: after 391, not later than 420, dated by nothing

errata.was: The Sun first rises; Dagor-nuin-Giliath; death of Fëanor
errata.why: 1 -- a conflation across an epoch Finding 394/395.

errata.now: Music of the Ainur; the Valar enter Eä (both before the count of years) — the Lamps are LATER and dated: AAm §14 sets them up in V.Y. 1900, 'Illuin and Ormal they were named. 1900 And they were set upon mighty pillars'; how long they stood is unstated
errata.was: Music of the Ainur; the Valar enter Eä; the Lamps (duration unstated)
errata.why: The repair keeps the era for the Music and the entering of Ea, which do precede the count, and gives the Lamps their annal year with the sentence that dates them.

errata.now: TWO Noldorin arrivals, an age apart: Feanor's host reached Lake Mithrim in Y.T. 1497, 'before the rising of the Moon' (GA, HoME XI); Fingolfin's came 'at the first rising of the Moon' (Silm 9) and held the north-west, and it is his realm this series follows
errata.was: The Noldor land in Mithrim; Fingolfin holds the north-west
errata.why: and blew their trumpets in Middle-earth at the first rising of the Moon." Both hosts were in Hithlum, so the realm's own phase series could not select between them -- which is what 413 retracted from 412.

errata.now: Father: ORODRETH (the owner's ruling, 1 Aug 2026), following HoME XII, The Shibboleth of Feanor — the latest manuscript. THE PARENTAGE MOVED THREE TIMES AND THE ARCHIVE SHOWS ALL THREE. (1) An addition of uncertain date to the Quenta (HoME XI.242) makes him FELAGUND's son: 'But foreseeing evil he commanded Orodreth to send away his son Gilgalad, and wife' — struck out, and undone by the Grey Annals of 1951, where 'Felagund had no wife, for the Vanya Amarie whom he loved had not been permitted to leave Aman'. (2) The published Silmarillion makes him FINGON's son — an editorial construction of Christopher Tolkien's, which he later regretted; the Silmarillion index still reads 'Ereinion: Scion of Kings, the son of Fingon'. (3) The Shibboleth makes him ORODRETH's son, Orodreth himself being moved from son of Finarfin to son of Angrod. The archive follows (3) and does not hide (1) or (2).

errata.now: IT IS 'THE FEANORIAN ALPHABET' (parts 1 and 2) AND 'ELDARIN PERSONAL PRONOUNS', both by Tolkien, edited by Arden R. Smith and Christopher Gilson -- established 2026-07-31 from the volume's own running heads after OCR, and NOT from anybody's memory. This entry previously read 'THE ARCHIVE CANNOT SAY WHAT IS IN IT ... every further description would be a guess', which was the right thing to write while it was a 152-page scan with no text layer. IT SERVES TWO HALLS AT ONCE and that is unusual: the Feanorian Alphabet is writing-systems material -- the volume opens with tengwar mode charts, one captioned 'Beleriandic Mode' -- and Eldarin Personal Pronouns is grammar. Its own numbers say the same: 284 hits for 'verb', 169 for 'consonant', 137 for 'Quenya'. EXTRACTION: OCR-DERIVED, 73,539 words at 300 dpi. The tengwar charts survive as noise, necessarily -- a scan of a non-Latin script read by a Latin-script engine -- so the CHARTS are evidence that material is there and are not themselves readable.
errata.was: EXTRACTION: SILENTLY MISSING -- an image-only scan, 152pp and 143 MB, no text layer on pages 1, 10, 50 or 100. THE ARCHIVE CANNOT SAY WHAT IS IN IT. It is held, it is a genuine issue of the modern series, and every further description would be a guess -- so this entry makes none.

errata.now: As Pictures. Carries Tolkien's own working maps and the note-sheets behind them, which the gazetteer's coordinates are measured against. Of the four art volumes the archive now holds, only Pictures by J.R.R. Tolkien came with a text layer; the other three are scans, which is what an art book usually is and why the captions -- the half the artwork ruling permits -- are the hardest half to obtain. errata.now: Words, Phrases and Passages in Various Tongues in The Lord of the Rings — Tolkien's own late commentary on every scrap of Elvish in the book, and the single most important linguistic source outside the Etymologies. THIS REGISTER NAMED IT AS THE CHIEF ABSENCE and it is now held. EXTRACTION: OCR-DERIVED, 123,801 words at 300 dpi, 2026-07-31. The most wanted volume on this shelf is readable at last -- and the archive can now say exactly how far to trust it, because it holds an INDEPENDENT CLEAN CONTROL for this one volume. GIRAUDEAU'S TWO DERIVED INDICES (t3) list 474 distinct Quenya headwords drawn from PE17, each carrying a [PE17:page] citation -- 3,256 citations reaching 176 of these 221 pages. Checking them against the OCR splits exactly along the diacritic: PLAIN FORMS 215 of 364 survive (59.1%); ACCENTED FORMS 10 of 110 (9.1%). A 6.5x difference, measured against somebody else's clean text rather than against my own sample of VT39. Anduril, Elentari, Endore, Finarato, Lorien, Melcore and Poldorea are all listed by Giraudeau and all lost here. SO THE DERIVED INDEX CAN RESCUE THE SOURCE IT WAS DERIVED FROM: he supplies the correct spelling AND the page it stands on, which is a repair route this shelf did not have before both volumes were held. Until that repair is made and checked, this file is commentary and not orthography.
errata.was: Words, Phrases and Passages in Various Tongues in The Lord of the Rings — Tolkien's own late commentary on every scrap of Elvish in the book, and the single most important linguistic source outside the Etymologies. THIS REGISTER NAMED IT AS THE CHIEF ABSENCE and it is now held. EXTRACTION: SILENTLY MISSING -- an image-only scan, 221pp, no text layer on any page sampled. The most wanted volume on this shelf is held and unreadable, and that is the plainest statement of where §1 actually stands.

The quotation is given from mid-sentence because a footnote marker stands inside the full clause ('were crowned with elanor 20 and sweet lissuin'); the flowers were brought by the Elves of Eressëa to the WEDDING feast of Aldarion and Erendis, at Andúnië — 'Thus the Eldar graced the wedding of Erendis... Their ship was laden with flowers for the adornment of the feast, so that all that sat there, when evening was come, were crowned with elanor and sweet lissuin.' This record said 'betrothal' until 29 July 2026; the betrothal was a separate and earlier event, at which Meneldur's gift to Erendis was land in Emerië, not flowers.

errata.now: The corpus never names her, and that clause is exact: across tiers 1 and 2 the only entry for her is an index line, "'Tradition of Isildur'; Isildur's wife." What it does record of her is not what this entry used to say. She did sail — when Sauron took Minas Ithil in S.A. 3429, Isildur 'went with his wife and his sons by ship down the River, and they sailed from the mouths of Anduin seeking Elendil', which the Tale of Years reads as 'sails north from Anduin's Mouths to Elendil in Arnor, with his wife and sons'. But the youngest son was not aboard: 'Valandil son of Isildur' was 'born in Imladris' the year after, in 3430. And the corpus leaves her in the north-east, not the south — 'his wife and his youngest son, Valandil, he had left in Imladris when he went to the war', and Isildur was riding to Imladris, 'for he had left his wife and youngest son there', when he was killed at the Gladden Fields. The southward sailing belongs to a different pair: in the Akallabêth 'Isildur and Anárion were borne away southwards' out of the Downfall — two brothers, and no wife in the sentence.
errata.was: She sailed south from the wreck of the realm with the youngest son — the corpus never names her.
errata.why: The only index entry for her at all is corpus/t1_d_unfinished_tales...:14070-14071 - "'Tradition of Isildur'; Isildur's wife." The rest of the sentence was wrong, and the passage that settles it is corpus/t1_a_the_silmarillion.txt:13330-13331: "his wife and his youngest son, Valandil, he had left in Imladris when he went to the war".

errata.now: She is named once, and the name belongs to Felagund — not to Orodreth. In The War of the Jewels an addition to QS §137, made “after the words 'he [Felagund] gave to Barahir his ring'”, reads that he 'sent away his wife Meril to her own folk in Eglorest, and with her went their son, yet an elvenchild, and Gilgalad Starlight he was called'. Christopher Tolkien glosses it on the next line — 'Felagund's wife Meril has not been named before, nor any child of his' — and the volume's index agrees: 'Meril  Wife of Felagund.' In the Orodreth variant, on the same page, she is NOT named: that note, struck out, reads only 'he commanded Orodreth to send away his son Gilgalad, and wife', and of a third note CT writes 'A blank space is here left for the name of Felagund's wife.' The late Peoples of Middle-earth text, which does make Gil-galad the son of Orodreth, likewise leaves her unnamed: 'Their mother was a Sindarin lady of the North. She called her son Gil-galad.' Under the published descent from Fingon, no mother is named at all.
errata.was: She is named once. In the War of the Jewels variant where Gil-galad is Orodreth's son, Orodreth 'sent away his wife MERIL to her own folk in Eglorest, and with her went their son, yet an elvenchild, and Gilgalad Starlight he was called'. The late Peoples of Middle-earth text keeps her unnamed: 'Their mother was a Sindarin lady of the North. She called her son Gil-galad.' Under the published descent from Fingon, no mother is named at all.
errata.why: Meril was Felagund's wife, and the entry gave her to Orodreth LORE_QUEUE.md, arda_silences entry 13 - MISCITED, right passage, wrong subject.

errata.now: Client-kingdoms, rumour, and one real account. No map, no census, no city-count and no homeland survey — but not nothing, and Khand is the proof. The corpus gives it a location, 'Khand  Land south-east of Mordor'; a people, 'Variags  The people of Khand'; a diplomacy — the Wainriders 'were in conflict with the peoples of Khand and their neighbours further south. Eventually a peace and alliance was agreed between these enemies of Gondor'; a dated war, the assault of 1944, in which they 'made alliance with men of Khand and of Near Harad; and in this great assault from north and south, Gondor came near to destruction'; and a place on the field, 'Easterlings with axes, and Variags of Khand'. Nor is the East wholly unrecorded: PoME says of the two Blue Wizards, there named Morinehtar and Rómestámo, that they 'must have had very great influence on the history of the Second Age and Third Age in weakening and disarraying the forces of East'. Tolkien's note reads 'the forces of East', without the article, and is quoted here as it stands. What is missing is a narrative and a set of numbers, not every trace.
errata.was: Client-kingdoms, rumour, and one real account. No map, no census, and nothing at all of Khand — but the East is not wholly unrecorded: PoME says of the two Blue Wizards, there named Morinehtar and Rómestámo, that they 'must have had very great influence on the history of the Second Age and Third Age in weakening and disarraying the forces of East'. Tolkien's note reads 'the forces of East', without the article, and is quoted here as it stands. What is missing is a narrative, not every trace.
errata.why: NOT CHANGED - the Blue Wizards half of the entry, repaired in its own commit; entry 1, "What are the populations of Harad, Rhûn and Khand?", which contains no overclaim - its text is "never a census, a city-count, or a homeland survey", and its Morannon citation stands.

errata.route: How do Orcs reproduce — and are there female Orcs?
errata.field: q=How do Orcs reproduce — and are there female Orcs?.a
path: q=How do Orcs reproduce — and are there female Orcs?
errata.now: HoME X says they 'had life and multiplied after the manner of the Children of Ilúvatar', and Myths Transformed in the same volume says a good deal more. They 'bred and multiplied rapidly whenever left undisturbed'; they 'needed food and drink, and rest'; and their lifespan is stated outright — 'they died and were not immortal, even according to the manner of the Quendi; indeed they appear to have been by nature short-lived compared with the span of Men of higher race, such as the Edain'. One mode of breeding is named too, of Men reduced to the Orc-level: 'they would or could be made to mate with Orcs, producing new breeds, often larger and more cunning'. What is genuinely undescribed is a female Orc — no she-orc, orc-woman or orc-mother appears as whole words in any of the 49 volumes, and a tier-3 encyclopedia reached the same finding: 'Nothing is said about Orkish tribal structures or female Orcs.'
errata.was: HoME X says they 'had life and multiplied after the manner of the Children of Ilúvatar'; no female orc, family, or lifespan is anywhere described.
errata.why: The passage that settles it, corpus/t1_10_morgoths_ring.txt:15534-15537, Myths Transformed: 15534 They could be slain, and they were subject to disease; 15535 but apart from these ills they died and were not immortal, even according to 15536 the manner of the Quendi; indeed they appear to have been by nature short- 15537 lived compared with the span of Men of higher race, such as the Edain.

errata.now: STILL NOT HELD. The text is Tolkien's and carries tier-1 authority; the journals are the Estate-permitted vehicle.

errata.now: She is named once. In the War of the Jewels variant where Gil-galad is Orodreth's son, Orodreth 'sent away his wife MERIL to her own folk in Eglorest, and with her went their son, yet an elvenchild, and Gilgalad Starlight he was called'. The late Peoples of Middle-earth text keeps her unnamed: 'Their mother was a Sindarin lady of the North. She called her son Gil-galad.' Under the published descent from Fingon, no mother is named at all.
errata.was: Three fathers across three drafts — and in no version, ever, a mother named.
errata.why: Gil-galad's mother is named Meril; Cuivienen's location stands in the same sentence used to prove it unknown; Tolkien answers the fate of the Entwives in the Letters and then retracts the answer, and the archive now holds both.

errata.now: The Dwarf-trade of Nogrod and Belegost ran through Caranthir's hands — “all the traffic of the dwarf-mines passed first through the hands of Caranthir, and thus great riches came to him”. No toll or tariff is recorded: the profit is stated, the mechanism is not.
errata.was: The Dwarf-trade monopoly: 'Caranthir's people... had the profit' of the traffic of Nogrod and Belegost — the recorded toll-taking makes this the most explicitly commercial Elvish realm.
errata.why: Six realm dossiers had quotation marks around words Tolkien never wrote; they now carry his actual sentences, and where the archive had invented a mechanism -- a toll at Thargelion, coal at Erebor, 'much traffic' in Gondor -- the claim is either corrected or marked inference.

errata.now: Haleth's folk hold Brethil free, on the one condition that they guard the Crossings of Teiglin — “that she should dwell free in Brethil, upon the condition only that her people should guard the Crossings of Teiglin”. The grant was obtained for her by Felagund: Thingol “would have denied it to Haleth”.
errata.was: By leave of Thingol they hold the wood 'free of tribute' on condition of guarding the Crossings — an explicit canonical treaty with terms.
errata.why: Brethil was not granted by Thingol's leave; Felagund obtained it, and Thingol would have denied it.

errata.now: Scale calibrated on Bag End to Rivendell — but that figure is NOT Tolkien's; he nowhere gives the distance. It derives from Fonstad's Atlas ('slightly more than 400 miles') and is a tier-3 reconstruction [T3]. Tolkien's own distances, usable as a check: 45 leagues Rivendell–Eregion; 102 leagues Edoras–Mundburg; 42 leagues Pelargir–the landings.

errata.why: The living map no longer claims Tolkien's authority for its scale.
